This study introduces SaliencyMix, a data augmentation technique that leverages the interpretability of saliency maps to enhance contrastive learning. By blending a reference image with its augmented counterpart based on saliency maps, SaliencyMix generates superior data augmentations compared to conventional methods. We further demonstrate that the saliency maps employed in SaliencyMix offer valuable interpretability, effectively highlighting the regions of the input image that drive the model's predictions.

We construct a class of quantum groups that are extensions of the affine Weyl group, denoted as $G_{n,r}$. These groups yield commutative quantum groups, and their bi-invariant functions form a convolution algebra isomorphic to the polynomial ring in $n r$ variables. We define a Hopf algebra structure on this ring, establishing it as a quantization of the bi-invariant functions defined on the classical Lie group $GL_{n,r}(\mathbb{C})$.

Cosmic shear surveys are essential for constraining cosmological parameters, yet they are susceptible to biases arising from intrinsic alignments of galaxies. While previous studies have established that these alignments are not random, they are instead linked to the local matter density field, the most significant of these being the "shape relaxation" effect. This phenomenon occurs because galaxies within dense regions tend to align with the local tidal field, creating a correlation between intrinsic shapes and the matter density field. This paper investigates how such intrinsic shape correlations influence the interpretation of cosmic shear data. We demonstrate that these correlations can induce a bias in the inferred cosmological parameters, with the magnitude of this bias depending on the specific cosmological model employed. Furthermore, we propose a method to mitigate this bias by utilizing the alignment of galaxies with the local tidal field to correct the measured shear correlations.

This study examines the large-strain response of soft-deformable particle systems, specifically those with shear-thinning properties, using a model featuring a nonlinear spring network. We analyze the system's behavior across various strain rates and particle numbers, observing that shear stress exhibits a non-monotonic trend with respect to mechanical energy. Furthermore, we investigate the system's relaxation dynamics following the cessation of shear, revealing a universal scaling law for the stress relaxation curve.

This study introduces a highly efficient machine learning force field designed for gold nanoparticles, utilizing a graph neural network architecture. The model was trained on a dataset comprising 1,000 molecular dynamics simulations of gold clusters containing 100 to 1,000 atoms, with each simulation lasting 100 picoseconds. The resulting force field accurately reproduces the structural and energetic characteristics of gold nanoparticles, including their radial distribution functions, density profiles, and energy components. Furthermore, the model demonstrates robust transferability, successfully predicting the structural and energetic properties of gold nanoparticles with up to 10,000 atoms without requiring additional training data.

This paper establishes bifurcation theorems regarding solutions that admit a variational character, derived from a spectral property associated with linearized equations. These findings generalize previous research conducted by the same author.

Grand unification (GU) and family triad (FT) are two foundational concepts in particle physics. GU posits that the gauge groups of the Standard Model unify into a single group at a high energy scale, while FT proposes that the three fermion families originate from a shared theoretical source. This work introduces a unified framework integrating GU and FT, specifically utilizing the $E_6$ grand unified model. In this approach, the Standard Model gauge group is embedded within $E_6}$, which contains an $SU(3)_\text{F}$ triad symmetry. This symmetry groups the three fermion families into a single multiplet of $E_6}$, thereby unifying GU and FT. The model is constructed using a single generation superfield, and the $SU(3)_\text{F}$ symmetry is broken by a GUT-scale Higgs field. This mechanism generates a Yukawa coupling matrix with a specific structure, enabling the calculation of fermion masses and mixing angles. The resulting mass spectrum aligns with experimental observations, and the mixing angles are consistent with data from neutrino oscillation experiments.
This study establishes novel relations for $(h; q)$-Genocchi numbers and polynomials by applying the ferbionic $h$-Stirling transform to $q$-Bernstein polynomials.

Randomized experiments are the gold standard for estimating treatment effects, yet their short-term nature often fails to capture long-term impacts, which are frequently more critical for decision-making. While recent literature has explored using machine learning to predict long-term outcomes from short-term experimental data, these methods typically rely on parametric models that struggle to capture complex, non-linear relationships. This paper introduces a novel framework for estimating long-term treatment effects by leveraging the flexibility of deep learning. We propose a new estimator that utilizes deep neural networks to model the conditional mean and variance of long-term outcomes based on short-term data. We establish theoretical bounds for the mean squared error of this estimator and validate our approach through simulations and a real-world application.

Case-control studies are frequently employed to investigate rare diseases, yet they are susceptible to recall bias, which compromises the accuracy of exposure data. This paper introduces a novel approach to correct bias in the odds ratio (OR) by leveraging data from a third, unbiased cohort study. The proposed method estimates the bias parameter using a weighted likelihood approach, where weights are derived from the odds ratio between cases and controls in the cohort study. The corrected OR is then calculated by adjusting the original estimate with this bias parameter. The method's performance is validated through a simulation study, and its practical utility is demonstrated by applying it to data from a study on multiple sclerosis.

Variational autoencoders (VAEs) have become a standard for learning latent representations, yet they often struggle with the complex data distributions found in real-world applications. To address this, we introduce Autoencoders within Flows (AEF), a framework that integrates normalizing flows into VAEs to generate a continuous, tractable, and highly flexible posterior distribution. By leveraging the differentiability of these flows, AEF can be trained end-to-end using maximum likelihood. Our results demonstrate that AEF outperforms conventional VAEs across various tasks, including image generation, image-to-image translation, and image classification.

Urban sensing involves gathering data from cities through various methods, such as mobile devices, sensors, and social media. This paper introduces a new approach to mining correlated attribute patterns (CAP) from urban sensing data, aiming to uncover relationships among attributes. We first define CAP and outline a mining algorithm based on the Apriori method. Additionally, we evaluate the algorithm's performance using both synthetic and real-world datasets. The results demonstrate that the algorithm is effective for identifying patterns and offers valuable insights for urban sensing applications.

This study introduces a novel hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method for solving two-dimensional reaction-diffusion equations, utilizing a stabilized approximation for the generalized Stokes equations as a foundational step. The proposed approach employs a stabilized HDG scheme to discretize the intermediate Stokes system, subsequently deriving an efficient, simplified, and computationally inexpensive discretization for the original reaction-diffusion problem. Theoretical analysis confirms that the final scheme achieves optimal convergence rates for both the velocity and pressure variables. Furthermore, numerical experiments are conducted to validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the method's computational efficiency.

Sensitivity analysis is a standard approach for addressing issues related to missing outcome data. This paper introduces a new sensitivity analysis framework designed to evaluate the impact of unobserved data on the estimated average treatment effect. The proposed method utilizes a flexible, non-parametric model to characterize the relationship between observed and unobserved outcomes, thereby enabling the generation of imputed values. This model is estimated using a Bayesian approach, which incorporates prior information regarding the missing data mechanism. The resulting sensitivity analysis is implemented within a multiple imputation structure, ensuring that the inherent uncertainty of the model is properly accounted for. The methodology is demonstrated through an application to a dataset from a randomized controlled trial.

This study introduces a Bayesian framework for analyzing gene expression data from crossover trials involving missing responses. The approach employs a linear mixed model to estimate gene effects, with the random effects and error terms following a multivariate t-distribution. This distribution is defined by a scale matrix and a vector of degrees of freedom, both of which are treated as unknown parameters. To address the missing data, we utilize a data augmentation technique that integrates the missing responses and their corresponding latent variables into the analysis. Additionally, we develop a Gibbs sampler to estimate the posterior distributions of all model parameters. The methodology is validated through a simulation study and applied to a clinical trial dataset involving the analysis of gene expression.

This paper presents a categorical definition of an $A_n$-structure, which serves as a higher-dimensional analogue to the definition of $A_\infty$-structures in 1-categories. We demonstrate that the category of $A_n$-structures within an $A_\infty$-category is itself endowed with an $A_\infty$-structure. Furthermore, we establish that the construction of this structure is both unique and natural.

DRAM reliability and performance can be significantly enhanced by leveraging its underutilized programmable internal timings. While prior research has primarily focused on adjusting these timings to boost reliability, this study introduces the first approach to harness them for performance gains. We demonstrate that DRAM's internal timing parameters can be tuned to accelerate data access, a method validated through a comprehensive analysis of the DRAM microarchitecture. This analysis reveals that DRAM exhibits distinct performance variations based on specific memory locations, a phenomenon caused by the interaction between program execution and memory access patterns. To address this, we developed a DRAM accelerator that optimizes these internal timings to minimize access latency. Our prototype, built on Intel's 3D XPoint technology, achieves a 1.5x speedup over standard DRAM. Furthermore, we integrated this accelerator into a DRAM-based main memory system, resulting in a 1.2x performance improvement on a real-world workload.

Network Functions Virtualization (NFV) enables the virtualization of network functions, allowing them to run on standard, off-the-shelf servers. This shift transforms traditional network operations into a software-driven environment, where Virtual Network Functions (VNFs) are instantiated on virtual infrastructure. This paper introduces a novel, self-organizing, and self-healing control framework designed to manage VNFs within NFV environments. The proposed architecture leverages a multi-agent system to handle VNF lifecycle management, specifically focusing on orchestration and placement. By utilizing a multi-agent system, the framework achieves self-organization and self-healing capabilities. The paper also details the design of a specific control agent and outlines the proposed VNF orchestration and placement strategy.

This study introduces a fault-tolerant quantum error correction scheme that leverages the full capabilities of multi-qubit gates to enhance efficiency. By utilizing a single Toffoli gate, the proposed method enables the creation of a surface code logical qubit with a minimal footprint of just 9 physical qubits. This approach significantly reduces the count of non-Clifford gates and T-depth within the error correction cycle, thereby lowering the system's susceptibility to errors. Additionally, the scheme employs a novel technique for fault-tolerant state preparation that uses a single Toffoli gate to generate a logical |++⟩ state, further diminishing the demand for non-Clifford gates.

OPUS, an open-source Python framework, is designed to facilitate the integration of diverse analysis and simulation tools. It enables the execution of multi-physics simulations and the analysis of experimental data, with a specific focus on nuclear fusion applications. Built on a modular architecture, OPUS allows users to easily incorporate new tools and adapt existing ones. The system's functionality is driven by a comprehensive set of abstract classes that define the interfaces for various tools, ensuring that each tool implements these specifications. This design allows for the seamless integration of tools from different origins, including those written in Python or those requiring external libraries. The paper details the system's architecture, implementation, and usage, supported by a demonstration of a multi-physics simulation of a tokamak plasma.

This paper introduces a novel digital game-based learning (DGBL) framework designed to enhance undergraduate engineering education. The study evaluates the framework's effectiveness by comparing it against traditional teaching methods, specifically examining its impact on student engagement, academic performance, and the acquisition of practical skills. The results demonstrate that the proposed DGBL approach significantly boosts student involvement and overall grades, while also fostering the development of essential practical abilities.

This study examines the atmospheric composition of Mars and Earth, specifically focusing on the relationship between molecular oxygen (O2) and ozone (O3). We developed a one-dimensional photochemical model to simulate the Martian atmosphere, utilizing the Mars Global Surveyor's UVS data for solar ultraviolet radiation. Our findings indicate that O2 and O3 are generated through photochemical processes in the Martian atmosphere, with O3 production rates showing a strong linear correlation to O2 concentrations. Additionally, we observed that O3 production rates increase with rising solar activity, whereas O2 production rates remain largely unaffected by solar variability.

We introduce a three-dimensional lattice framework designed to support stable, two-dimensional robust crosscurrents that are insensitive to lattice disorder. This system is realized by integrating a three-dimensional quantum Hall state with a three-dimensional topological superconductor. The crosscurrent's robustness stems from the topological protection of the quantum Hall state, which ensures stability against bulk impurities. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these crosscurrents exhibit a quantized Hall conductance, a property that remains invariant under two-dimensional lattice defects.

Neural machine translation systems trained across multiple languages have demonstrated the ability to enhance translation quality for languages with limited resources. This study evaluates the effectiveness of multilingual models in translating from the Kinyarwanda and Kirundi languages. We introduce a new dataset comprising 1,000 sentences for both Kinyarwanda and Kirundi, sourced from parallel translations of the English versions of the News Commentary corpus. Additionally, we assess the performance of m2m-100, a multilingual model developed by Facebook AI Research, on these Kinyarwanda and Kirundi translation tasks.

This study examines the generation of ion-acoustic waves within a dusty plasma environment, specifically accounting for the effects of positrons and non-thermal electrons. The analysis employs a reductive perturbation technique to derive the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation, which governs the nonlinear evolution of these waves. The resulting KdV equation is solved numerically to produce both solitary and periodic solutions. The findings indicate that the system's solitary and periodic waves are primarily driven by the presence of positively charged dust particles. Furthermore, the study concludes that the KdV equation accurately models the nonlinear behavior of ion-acoustic waves in such systems, with the specific characteristics of the waves being contingent upon the non-thermal nature of the electrons.

Recent developments in dense retrieval have demonstrated that leveraging pretrained language models (PLMs) to generate document embeddings can significantly boost performance. However, the computational demands of PLMs often render them impractical for real-time applications. To address this, we introduce a new method for generating document embeddings that bypasses PLMs entirely. Our approach utilizes a lightweight, end-to-end trainable model to predict the relevance scores of PLMs based solely on input query and document pairs. By training this predictor to mimic PLM behavior, we achieve retrieval performance comparable to state-of-the-art PLM-based baselines while drastically reducing latency. Our experiments on the MS MARCO dataset confirm that our method attains performance on par with leading PLMs, yet it operates at a fraction of the computational cost.

Multimodal learning (MML) seeks to integrate information from diverse sources, such as text and images, to enhance performance on complex tasks. However, existing MML methods often fail to fully leverage the complementary strengths of different modalities, leading to suboptimal outcomes. To address this, we introduce a new framework called Multimodal Learning with Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation (MML-KD). This approach utilizes a teacher network trained on a single modality to guide the learning of a student network across multiple modalities. By employing a teacher-student architecture, MML-KD facilitates the transfer of knowledge between modalities, thereby enhancing the student's ability to learn effectively. Empirical results demonstrate that MML-KD surpasses current state-of-the-art methods on various multimodal tasks, including image captioning and visual question answering.

We investigate the relativistic quantum dynamics of massless fermions within a noncommutative spacetime, focusing on the vector and axial vector two-point functions. By analyzing the ultraviolet divergences in these functions, we derive the corresponding renormalization constants.

This study introduces a novel end-to-end spoken command recognition system utilizing a tensor-train (TT) network. It employs a TT-structured convolutional neural network (CNN) to process input audio data, leveraging the inherent TT structure to significantly reduce the model's parameter count. Furthermore, the proposed architecture incorporates a tensor-train recurrent neural network (RNN) to capture temporal dependencies within the data. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on the DCASE 2020 Task 11 command detection challenge.

We introduce a comprehensive framework for unraveling open quantum systems, which encompasses all known quantum-jump approaches and extends to numerous novel ones. This framework is formulated as a quantum-classical hybrid stochastic process, where the quantum evolution is conditioned on the trajectory of the classical component. The text provides an exact characterization of the class of master equations compatible with such processes, alongside a corresponding classification of the associated stochastic generators. Additionally, the authors present a specific class of these equations that admits a minimal unraveling featuring only two distinct jump types.

Light absorption in solar cells is significantly influenced by the morphology of nanoparticles (NPs) embedded within the active layer. This study investigates how NP shape impacts light absorption in a perovskite solar cell (PSC) utilizing a single-layer architecture. We demonstrate that spherical NPs yield the highest absorption across the entire solar spectrum, followed by ellipsoidal and cubic NPs in descending order. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of NP size on absorption, revealing that larger NPs enhance light absorption more effectively than smaller ones.

We introduce a novel logical framework capable of characterizing functions solvable in deterministic polynomial time. This logic extends first-order language with a fixed-point mechanism, mirroring the approach used for defining P in previous research. However, our extension differs by incorporating a specific operator designed to guarantee termination within a polynomial number of steps. We demonstrate that any function definable in this system can indeed be computed in polynomial time. Conversely, we establish that every deterministic polynomial-time computable function can be expressed using our proposed logic.

LSTMs are widely utilized in natural language processing, yet their inherent complexity often hampers training efficiency and inference speed. This study introduces a novel LSTM architecture designed to reduce parameter count and computational load while preserving accuracy. We achieve this by integrating a skip-connection mechanism that enables the model to learn from both current and previous hidden states. Additionally, we employ a dynamic gating strategy to selectively activate hidden states based on the specific task, further lowering complexity. Our approach is evaluated on the English WikiText-103 dataset, where it demonstrates superior performance compared to standard LSTMs and existing variants, achieving higher accuracy with fewer parameters.

MAVLink serves as the primary communication protocol for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), facilitating data exchange between various subsystems. However, it suffers from significant security flaws, including the lack of authentication, encryption, and mechanisms to ensure message integrity. This paper introduces a novel, lightweight security framework designed to address these issues. The proposed solution employs a shared secret key to authenticate messages and utilizes a key exchange protocol to establish a secure channel for encrypted communication. The framework's security is validated through a series of experiments conducted on a physical UAV testbed.

The widespread adoption of large-scale distributed applications has made it essential to understand the characteristics of the underlying network. This paper introduces a framework designed to analyze network properties and their impact on such applications. By leveraging extensive data from the Linux kernel, the framework enables the analysis of network attributes across both individual hosts and the broader network. It offers a comprehensive view of network behavior, ranging from packet-level details to aggregate flows, and can be applied to both live systems and historical data. The framework's utility is demonstrated through two case studies: first, examining how network properties affect the performance of a large-scale distributed application, and second, identifying network anomalies by analyzing their effects on traffic patterns.

We demonstrate that self-dual solutions of vacuum Maxwell equations defined on a four-dimensional conformally flat background map to specific solutions of Einstein's equations exhibiting a Hodge duality property within the same context. This correspondence is established by treating both the Maxwell and gravitational fields as curvature forms of their respective principal bundles.

This paper introduces a novel muon tomography method designed to map the internal structure of concrete. By analyzing the trajectories of muons passing through the material, the technique identifies internal voids and cavities. The study examines the tomographic reconstruction of a 1.5 m³ concrete block containing three distinct cavities. Results indicate that the tomographic images successfully delineate the voids' locations and dimensions with high precision.

Parsing Expression Grammars (PEGs) are a formalism for defining context-free languages, where ordered recursive choice serves as a primary mechanism. This feature mandates that when multiple alternatives match an input, only the first successful option is selected. This paper introduces a novel extension to PEGs that incorporates a new operator for "unconstrained choice," allowing any matching option to be picked regardless of evaluation order. This operator is defined through a generalized version of the matching relation, which is extended to accommodate sets of alternatives rather than single options. We demonstrate that this generalized relation is sufficient to express both ordered and unconstrained choices, as well as a broader class of operators that permit a predetermined limit on the number of alternatives that can be tried.

We calculate the Cherenkov radiation rate of a time-dependent electric field within a thermal medium, specifically for the high-temperature regime. The findings indicate that the rate diminishes exponentially as temperature increases beyond a certain threshold.

This study investigates the application of predictability metrics, derived from sophisticated neural language models, to analyze EEG signals during language tasks. We evaluated these measures against established metrics like surprisal and lexical frequency to determine their efficacy in modeling EEG responses during sentence reading. Results indicate that predictability scores from advanced language models align more closely with EEG data than those from less complex models or traditional metrics. Furthermore, we examined the relationship between neural responses and semantic processing by contrasting the predictive performance of models with and without integrated word embeddings. Our findings reveal that models utilizing word embeddings are better suited for capturing neural correlates of semantic processing than those relying solely on one-hot encoded word forms.

This study introduces a new dataset comprising 1,000 video clips featuring 3D object pose estimation for 1,000 distinct objects. Unlike prior collections that rely on studio-captured videos of a single object against a plain background, our dataset consists of authentic recordings of objects in natural environments. These videos offer significant advantages for single-view 3D pose estimation, as they encompass a diverse range of object instances, orientations, and lighting conditions. To facilitate this, we developed a semi-automatic pipeline that leverages existing 3D models and 2D pose annotations to automatically generate 3D pose estimates for every frame. The resulting dataset is publicly available at https://github.com/PrincetonUniversity/3D-Object-Pose-Estimation-in-the-Wild.

Semiconductor-superconductor heterostructures hosting Andreev bound states (ABS) are recognized as promising platforms for investigating quantum spin Hall states and Majorana bound states. This study examines the coupling between ABS and edge states in quantum Hall systems. We demonstrate that ABS in such hybrid structures can facilitate coupling between edge states of opposite chiralities via two mechanisms: direct tunneling and Andreev reflection. Furthermore, we show that ABS can induce coupling between edge states of the same chirality through Andreev reflection. Consequently, these findings suggest that semiconductor-superconductor heterostructures are ideal for investigating the interaction between ABS and quantum Hall edge states.

Magnetic reconnection serves as a primary mechanism for energizing particles within various astrophysical plasmas, including solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and active galactic nuclei. This study examines the particle acceleration dynamics in a two-dimensional reconnection scenario featuring a guide field, utilizing a hybrid model that incorporates kinetic effects for ions and fluid behavior for electrons. The simulation employs a particle-in-cell (PIC) method for ions and a finite-volume approach for electrons. Results indicate that ions gain energy through betatron acceleration, while electrons are energized via direct electric field acceleration. Furthermore, the study analyzes the relationship between the magnetic field and the distribution of accelerated particles.

We investigate the one-loop corrections to the Higgsstrahlung process ($e^+e^- \to ZH$) within a model featuring an extended scalar sector. Our analysis focuses on the impact of a light scalar singlet on the renormalization of the $Z$ boson mass and the $Z$-fermion couplings. We demonstrate that these effects are substantial, particularly when the scalar singlet mass is low. Furthermore, we calculate the corresponding corrections to the $e^+e^- \to ZH$ cross-section and establish the associated theoretical uncertainties.

This paper investigates the definition of the subgradient for the joint numerical radius of pairs of operators. It establishes a characterization for when this set is non-empty. Furthermore, the study defines the infimal joint numerical radius and provides a criterion for its non-emptiness.

Recent years have seen deep learning frameworks increasingly adopted for financial trading, particularly in forecasting asset prices and analyzing market trends. However, the heavy reliance on large datasets for model training introduces significant privacy and security challenges. This paper introduces a novel approach to train deep learning models using distributed data without exposing the underlying raw information. By leveraging homomorphic encryption, we enable the direct execution of deep learning computations on encrypted data. Our methodology involves a specialized neural network architecture capable of handling encrypted inputs and weights, allowing for the training of models across multiple parties with locally partitioned data. We validate this approach using a distributed LSTM network designed to predict stock prices. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves prediction accuracy comparable to standard training methods, confirming the viability of deploying deep learning on encrypted distributed datasets.

This study examines the framework of second-order stochastic processes for multivariate functions, alongside the corresponding Hilbert-Schmidt integral operators. We demonstrate that these integral operators form a reproducing kernel structure. Additionally, we establish a connection between these integral operators and the multivariate second-order stochastic mappings, and we derive the associated multivariate Karhunen–Loève expansions.

This study introduces a novel ignition mechanism for hydrogen-oxygen mixtures at high pressures, driven by the synergistic effects of thermal and electrical discharges. The research examines the ignition characteristics of such mixtures under varying conditions of pressure, gap distance, and discharge energy. The findings reveal that the minimum energy required for ignition decreases significantly as the discharge gap widens, a trend that becomes even more pronounced at higher pressures. The ignition process is attributed to the thermal explosion of the gas caused by seed electrons generated via the Townsend avalanche effect. The paper further analyzes the roles of both thermal and electrical discharges in this ignition process, demonstrating that thermal explosion is the primary driver, while electrical discharge acts as a crucial facilitator.

This paper introduces a Boundary-Aware Segmentation Network (BASN), designed to deliver precise segmentation by integrating three core components: a multi-scale feature extraction module, a boundary-aware feature fusion module, and a segmentation head. The multi-scale feature extraction module employs a multi-scale attention mechanism to capture both local and global context, thereby enhancing the representation of semantic features. The boundary-aware feature fusion module utilizes a specialized attention mechanism to isolate and refine boundary information, ensuring the network can accurately distinguish object edges. Finally, the segmentation head combines these processed features to generate the ultimate segmentation output. Extensive experiments on the Pascal VOC 2012 benchmark demonstrate that BASN achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing existing methods.

Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication offers a promising avenue for enhancing the situational awareness of Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) by sharing data with other road users. This paper introduces a novel framework for CAVs to generate a comprehensive, 3D view of their surroundings by integrating data from both direct perception and V2X interactions. The proposed method employs a 3D point cloud to represent the environment, utilizing a 3D Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) to model the probability distribution of points within the cloud. This probabilistic approach enables the system to effectively handle uncertainty inherent in perception and communication processes. Furthermore, the system leverages 3D Gaussian Mixture Models to merge point clouds derived from on-board sensors with those received from neighboring vehicles. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach yields a more precise and reliable reconstruction of the environment compared to methods relying solely on either perception or V2X data.

This study investigates the behavior of two-dimensional active Brownian particles (ABPs) confined within a two-dimensional channel featuring a central obstacle. The system comprises two distinct groups of particles: a small number of strongly active particles and a larger population of weakly active ones. We analyze how varying the strength ratio and the concentration of these groups influences their spatial distribution and flow dynamics. Our findings reveal that increasing the activity of weakly active particles leads to a higher local density and intensified flow near boundaries, a phenomenon driven by the accumulation of particles against walls and the resulting enhancement of their effective activity.

The paper introduces a novel approach to describing electronic states in plasmas, utilizing a modified wave function that incorporates a complex potential. This method yields a complex energy value, which is split into two distinct components: a real part and an imaginary part. The real component corresponds to the energy of the state, whereas the imaginary part quantifies the rate of electron emission. These complex-energy eigenstates, referred to as Siegert states, offer a comprehensive description that encompasses both bound and continuum states, effectively superseding the conventional separation of these states. This methodology is applied to investigate electron emission from a hydrogen atom subjected to a static electric field.

This study examines the 2014 July 22 solar flare, which was observed by the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO) and the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA). The analysis focuses on the temporal and spatial evolution of the flare's soft X-ray (SXR) and extreme ultraviolet (EUV) emissions. We identified a recurring pattern in the intensity and velocity of the Fe XXIV 192 Å emission line, which we attribute to magnetic reconnection occurring in the flare's current sheet. Additionally, we detected a distinct "dip" in the Fe XXIV 192 Å emission line that coincides with the peak of the Fe XXIV 192 Å emission line. This dip is likely caused by the flare's chromospheric evaporation, which leads to the cooling of the plasma and a subsequent decrease in the emission line's intensity.

We investigate the impact of a topological theta term on the confinement of color fields within the framework of quantum chromodynamics (QCD). Our findings indicate that the inclusion of this term in the QCD action leads to confinement, a result derived from a perturbative analysis of the QCD vacuum. Specifically, we demonstrate that the vacuum energy density exhibits a quadratic dependence on the color field, a characteristic that generates a confining potential for color charges.

This study examines the influence of ion-beam irradiation on the surface morphology of a thin film, specifically focusing on the critical angle ($\theta_c$) that separates surface roughening from smoothing. The analysis utilizes a kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) model to simulate the evolution of surface topography under varying irradiation conditions. The results indicate that $\theta_c$ is contingent upon ion species, energy, and fluence. Furthermore, the paper derives an analytical expression for $\theta_c$ based on the parameters governing the KMC model. The study also investigates the relationship between the critical angle and the mean step height, demonstrating that $\theta_c$ decreases as step height increases. Additionally, the findings reveal that the critical angle is sensitive to the type of surface defects and the initial surface topography.

This study introduces a novel approach to source code anti-plagiarism that safeguards code integrity by ensuring the unaltered use of submitted code. The proposed method leverages two cryptographic primitives: hash functions and digital signatures. The first technique involves a two-stage process where the system generates a hash of the original code and transmits it to the user; the user then re-hashes the code upon submission and sends the resulting value back to the system. The system verifies the integrity by comparing the received hash against its original record. The second technique involves the system issuing a digital signature for the code, which the user returns alongside the submission for validation. The results indicate that both methods are effective in preventing plagiarism and unauthorized modifications.

We establish that for any Dirichlet series $F(s)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty a_n n^{-s}$ with coefficients satisfying $\sum_{n=1}^\infty |a_n|^2 < \infty$, the function $F(s)$ is analytic in the half-plane $\Re(s)>\frac12$. This result demonstrates that the series' growth order is bounded by its $L^2$ coefficient magnitude.

We establish that for any group $G$ and positive integers $k$ and $r$, there exists a finite subset $A \subset G$ such that the $k$-fold product set $A^k$ is contained within a $(k,r)$-multiplicative approximate subgroup $B$ of $G$. Specifically, $B$ satisfies the property that $xBx \subset B$ for all $x \in A$, and additionally, for every $g \in G$, the intersection $B \cap gBg^{-1}$ is non-empty.

This study addresses nonparametric inference for log-concave densities, a class of unimodal distributions characterized by concave log-density functions. We introduce a new estimator that leverages the convex geometry of the underlying data to achieve superior asymptotic efficiency compared to existing methods. The estimation process involves two primary steps: first, deriving a convex set of candidate densities that satisfy log-concavity constraints, and second, identifying the most probable density within this set by minimizing the empirical log-loss. We demonstrate that this new estimator is asymptotically more efficient than the standard Grenander estimator, which is derived from maximum likelihood estimation under unimodality assumptions. Furthermore, we establish the estimator's asymptotic normality and confirm that it attains the Cramér-Rao lower bound.

This study introduces a Wang-Landau algorithm designed to sample static configurations in two-dimensional frictionless granular systems, utilizing a modified density of states that accounts for the discreteness of particle positions. We demonstrate that this approach yields a uniform distribution of particle locations and accurately reproduces the correct static force-force correlation functions. Furthermore, the method is applied to investigate jamming in two-dimensional systems of frictionless disks, revealing that the Wang-Landau algorithm can generate jammed states with a packing fraction as high as $\phi=0.84$.

We introduce a novel two-player game, Explorer-Director, in which Explorer aims to locate a hidden target within a graph $G$ by issuing queries, while Director responds by selecting the answer. Explorer's objective is to minimize the worst-case number of queries required to guarantee finding the target. We demonstrate that for every graph $G$, a specific strategy exists that achieves an expected number of queries bounded by $O(\log n)$, where $n$ represents the count of vertices in $$G$.

This study examines the higher-order Broer-Kaup (HBK) system using the generalized bilinear method. Exact interaction solutions involving solitons, singular solitons, and algebraic waves are derived. By analyzing parameter constraints, we determine the conditions under which these different wave types emerge. Furthermore, three-dimensional plots are generated to visually represent the interaction dynamics among the various singular and solitonic waves.

We investigate the incompressible Euler equations within a periodic domain, specifically examining the scenario where vorticity is prescribed at a fixed time. We demonstrate that by manipulating the boundary velocity, one can achieve a final state with varying energy levels. Consequently, this finding indicates that energy preservation is not inherent to the Euler equations when vorticity is held fixed.

VIRUP is a virtual reality (VR) platform designed to enable users to explore and analyze vast datasets through an immersive 3D environment. It offers a user-friendly interface for navigating these data points, which are visualized as 3D objects within the virtual space. To ensure a seamless and engaging experience, the system employs a high-performance rendering engine that leverages the capabilities of modern graphics cards. Furthermore, the application is built on a modular architecture, allowing for the seamless integration of new visualization techniques and 3D rendering methods.

This paper introduces a data education framework tailored for young learners, leveraging physical objects like Lego bricks to create tangible data visualizations. By connecting these physical arrangements to digital representations, the method fosters a deeper understanding of data through the integration of physical and digital environments. We outline the design principles behind this approach, describe the development of a prototype system, and report on an initial evaluation conducted with children.

This paper addresses the challenge of identifying all viable operational data paths within a Software Defined Networking (SDN) environment. We introduce a novel algorithm that leverages the control plane to discover every feasible operational data path, provided the switch ports involved are active. The method relies on two necessary and sufficient conditions: first, the existence of a valid flow rule governing the ingress port of a switch, and second, the presence of an egress port connecting to a link. By verifying these criteria, the algorithm can comprehensively enumerate all operational data paths. We have implemented this approach in an OpenFlow-based SDN testbed, demonstrating its efficacy through a case study.

Although disentangling neural representations is a critical challenge, current approaches often fail to adequately address the inherent difficulties of enforcing disentanglement. This paper introduces a new method that leverages the concept of "intrinsic" disentanglement, which posits that the underlying factors of variation are naturally separable within the data manifold. By utilizing this principle, we develop a novel regularization technique that significantly enhances the disentanglement of latent codes. Empirical evaluations across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that our approach surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods.

This study examines the hydrodynamic performance of a two-foil arrangement designed for harvesting energy from currents. The analysis focuses on the impact of varying the distance between foils and the angle of attack on the efficiency of energy extraction. The research utilizes a numerical approach based on the Navier-Stokes equations, employing a finite volume method with second-order accuracy. The findings indicate that the efficiency of the tandem system is highly dependent on the spacing between foils and the angle of attack. Specifically, the efficiency peaks when the spacing-to-chord ratio is approximately 2.5 and the angle of attack is around 10 degrees.

We introduce a method to detect charge-tunneling events between a quantum dot and a superconducting island, utilizing a nearby quantum dot as a sensitive electrometer. This setup enables the measurement of Andreev reflection through the superconducting island by monitoring the Coulomb-blockade characteristics of the probe dot. Theoretically, we demonstrate that this approach can resolve Andreev reflection with a superconducting gap approximately 100 times larger than the energy resolution limit of the quantum dot electrometer.

Drug targets are crucial for disease pathogenesis and serve as the primary focus of pharmaceutical research. Although target identification is a key step in drug discovery, it remains a significant challenge. While recent advancements in deep learning have enabled the prediction of drug-target interactions, these models often fail to provide the specific drug targets necessary for disease treatment. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel framework for drug target prediction that integrates both disease and drug features. This approach utilizes a deep learning architecture based on graph convolutional networks (GCNs) to model the relationships between drugs and diseases. By leveraging the structural information inherent in the data, our method effectively predicts drug targets for various diseases. Experimental results demonstrate that this graph convolutional network-based framework outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

This paper examines implementation strategies for lambda-calculus, specifically focusing on the trade-offs between memory usage and execution speed. We analyze both call-by-name and call-by-value approaches, covering both explicit stack and implicit approaches. Our evaluation framework considers three key aspects: stack depth, the count of distinct locations within the explicit stack, and the number of pointers within the environment. We present novel strategies for both call-by-name and call-by-value scenarios, as well as a new method for the implicit stack call-by-value approach. Furthermore, we introduce a novel metric for assessing stack depth and the number of environment locations, and we demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed strategies through experimental results.

The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) and Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) represent a unique system of interacting galaxies, offering a rare chance to study how galactic interactions influence evolution. This study examines the stellar populations of both galaxies using the Hubble Space Telescope's Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS). We applied a Bayesian hierarchical model to ACS data from the LMC and SMC, utilizing a flexible parametric star formation history (SFH) to characterize the populations. Our SFHs were benchmarked against independent SFHs derived from the same ACS data using the pPXF method, as well as against SFHs from the MUSE Faint Galaxy Evolution Survey (MaNGA) and the Hubble Space Telescope's Wide Field Camera 3 (WFC3). The results indicate that the LMC and SMC share similar SFHs, with both galaxies experiencing a peak in star formation approximately 10 billion years ago. Smart grids are increasingly vulnerable to electricity theft, a challenge that undermines the efficiency of power distribution. This paper introduces a deep recurrent neural network designed to identify electricity theft by analyzing smart meter data. The proposed method utilizes a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to process smart meter readings, effectively capturing temporal dependencies within the data. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves superior performance compared to existing methods, yielding an accuracy of 99.99%.

This study presents a combinatorial characterization of minimal surface graphs defined on a torus. Leveraging this theoretical framework, we develop an algorithm to compute the corresponding typical canonical forms.

This study reports the first measurement of the $c$-baryon $\Omega^0_c$ lifetime, utilizing a dataset of $3.0\,\text{fb}^{-1}$ of $pp$ collisions collected by the LHCb experiment at center-of-mass energies of $7\,\text{TeV}$ and $8\,\text{TeV}$. The $\Omega^0_c$ baryon is identified through the decay channel $\Omega^- \to \Xi^- K^+$. The resulting lifetime is determined to be $\tau_{\Omega^0_c} = (210.5 \pm 6.4\,\text{(stat)} \pm 4.4\,\text{(syst)})\,\text{fs}$.

Subspace clustering has become a widely adopted unsupervised learning technique in remote sensing, particularly for tasks like land cover mapping and object detection. This paper introduces a novel approach that integrates the spectral clustering method with the sparse subspace clustering algorithm. By leveraging the sparse representation inherent in spectral clustering, we enhance the robustness of the clustering process. Furthermore, we develop a new objective function that unites the graph Laplacian from spectral clustering with the affinity matrix from sparse subspace clustering. This integration allows the model to effectively capture both global and local data structures. The proposed method is optimized using an iterative algorithm, and its efficacy is demonstrated through experiments on synthetic data and real-world remote sensing datasets.

The framework integrates a two-dimensional thermodynamic energy balance with a one-dimensional thermodynamic heat conduction equation, alongside a two-dimensional radiative transfer model. The latter simulates the interaction between solar radiation and sea ice, incorporating the effects of snow cover and ice albedo. We introduce a method to generate specific final states in atom-molecule ultracold scattering by applying dynamic magnetic fields. This approach relies on the Fano effect, which enables the selective creation of final outcomes through interference between a scattering pathway and a closed-loop transition-continuum cycle driven by the time-varying magnetic field. This technique is demonstrated using the system of a $^{87}$Rb atom colliding with an OH radical.

This study proposes a generalization of the standard Boltzmann-Gibks-IHuang (H) dynamics within nonextensive thermostatistics, utilizing a recently introduced operator for nonextensive statistics. We demonstrate that this newly proposed operator satisfies the detailed balance condition, a requirement essential for deriving the correct nonextensive equilibrium distribution.

We present a theoretical proposal for realizing Floquet Weyl semimetal states within a two-dimensional topological insulator subjected to periodic driving. This system supports unique topological features, including Floquet-Weyl nodes, nontrivial Chern numbers, and topological hinge modes. We further investigate the influence of various parameters on the resulting topological phase diagram.

This paper introduces a decentralized computing protocol designed to incentivize accurate computation and data processing. It achieves this by leveraging the inherent randomness found in the execution of distributed algorithms. The protocol's core mechanism involves a computation provider who offers a service to a client, with the client receiving a proof of the computation's completion. The validity of this proof is determined by a distributed algorithm's outcome, which is established through a randomized process. The client is assured that the probability of a false positive—incorrectly accepting a flawed proof—is bounded by a constant value that is strictly less than one.

Rate-Distortion Optimization (RDO) is a critical component of video coding, yet it remains a computationally demanding task. This challenge is particularly pronounced in 3D point clouds, where the vast number of points results in an excessive number of rate-distortion calculations. This paper introduces a novel, efficient method for RDO in 3D point clouds that leverages the spatial correlation inherent in the data. The proposed approach first segments the point cloud into multiple regions, then performs RDO calculations exclusively on the region containing the point of interest, while simultaneously estimating the rate-distortion values for the remaining areas. Experimental results indicate that this method achieves a 10x reduction in computational complexity with negligible impact on coding efficiency.

We investigate the QCD phase diagram at finite temperature and chemical potential using a chiral effective Lagrangian. Our analysis reveals that the critical lines for chiral symmetry breaking and deconfinement transitions intersect at a single point, a result consistent with findings from lattice QCD.

Obtaining ground truth annotations for medical images is often difficult and costly, which hinders the training of deep learning models. Self-supervised learning (SSL) offers a promising solution by enabling the training of deep networks without labeled data. This paper introduces a new self-supervised framework designed for medical image segmentation, leveraging the inherent structural information within these images. Our approach utilizes a self-supervised teacher to generate pseudo-labels, which are then used to train a student network. To ensure the quality of these pseudo-labels, we have developed a self-supervised consistency loss. Experimental results on the MICCAI 2020 "Segmentation of Abdominal Organs and Lesions" challenge demonstrate that our method achieves competitive performance compared to other approaches.

Unlike conventional font generation methods that require extensive training datasets, few-shot font generation aims to create new fonts using only a small number of examples. This study introduces a novel few-shot font generation framework that leverages the distinctive characteristics of font images. The approach employs a dual-stage process: first, it extracts the core structural information from character images to generate a font-specific structural prior, and second, it synthesizes new fonts by integrating this prior with a pretrained generative model. Experimental results demonstrate that this method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in few-shot font generation.

We investigate the impact of torsion on a charged fluid within the context of Einstein-Cartan-Kibble-Sciama (ECKS) gravity. By employing a Lagrangian framework, we derive the corresponding field equations and establish a consistent fluid description. Our analysis demonstrates that in stationary backgrounds, the interaction between the fluid and torsion generates non-vanishing spin vorticity and torsional current, which in turn induce a non-trivial spin vorticity pressure. Furthermore, we examine the thermodynamic properties of this fluid, specifically focusing on the behavior of the Hawking temperature and entropy density.

This study introduces a novel digital twin-assisted adaptive video streaming framework designed to enhance user experience. The approach involves building user-specific digital twins to forecast the future network conditions of individual users. These predictions are utilized to determine optimal video quality levels, thereby reducing the frequency of switching events. The paper details the construction of these digital twins, the methodology for estimating user models, and the specific mechanisms employed to select video quality based on predicted twin outputs. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed framework significantly lowers the switching rate while maintaining performance comparable to existing state-of-the-art solutions.

Neutrino astronomy has recently entered a new era, marked by the detection of high-energy neutrinos from blazars and the identification of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos. These sources are anticipated to produce neutrinos with energies spanning from the GeV to PeV scales. While the flavor composition of neutrinos originating from these sources is initially expected to be an equal mixture of electron, muon, and tau neutrinos, long-distance propagation induces oscillations that shift this ratio to approximately 1:1:1 upon arrival at Earth. This study examines the impact of these flavor oscillations on the observed energy spectra of astrophysical neutrinos, specifically analyzing the IceCube data to constrain the spectral shape of the neutrino flux from blazars. Our findings indicate that accounting for flavor oscillations is essential for accurately interpreting blazar neutrino data, as neglecting them can lead to incorrect conclusions regarding the source's spectral properties.

This paper examines the almost sure global wellposedness of the periodic nonlinear Schrödinger equation featuring either the cubic or quintic Hardy-type nonlinearity. We demonstrate that both the cubic and quintic forms of this nonlinearity yield almost sure global wellposedness given $L^2$ initial data.

This paper introduces a new framework for feedback control that enables humans to remotely operate machines over networks characterized by variable latency. The system is designed to support high-throughput data exchange and low-latency feedback, meeting the rigorous demands of teleoperation and haptics. It relies on three core pillars: (1) a human-machine interface (HMI) that delivers intuitive, real-time feedback; (2) a machine learning-based adaptive controller that dynamically adjusts to fluctuating network conditions; and (3) a network architecture capable of maintaining low latency and high throughput despite congestion. The study validates this approach through a teleoperation experiment involving a remote excavator, demonstrating its effectiveness in a real-world setting.

Sgr A East, a supernova remnant located in the Galactic center, is a well-documented object with an estimated age of 2–5 Myr. Its radio emission is notably intense, yet the source's X-ray counterpart remains unidentified. This study presents a new analysis of the X-ray emission from Sgr A East using data from the Chandra X-ray Observatory. We report a detection of the source at a significance level of 3.5σ, with a total count of 10.5 events. This count is consistent with the source's radio luminosity, suggesting a non-thermal origin for the X-rays. Additionally, we observed a significant correlation between the X-ray and radio fluxes, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.91.

The LHCb collaboration has recently reported findings from b-hadron decays that suggest a potential breach of lepton universality. This paper outlines the design and operational principles of the upgraded LHCb detector, specifically detailing the modifications implemented to enhance its capabilities for investigating these phenomena.

Although deep learning has achieved significant success in natural language processing, it has not yet reached the same level of success in discourse processing. This paper investigates the application of deep learning to discourse segmentation and connective detection. Our findings indicate that manually engineered features remain essential for achieving state-of-the-art results in these tasks. To address this, we introduce a hybrid model that integrates both deep learning and hand-crafted features. This approach yields substantial improvements over existing baselines, achieving new state-of-the-art performance on the CoNLL 2009 discourse segmentation dataset.

To meet the demands of upcoming network technologies, Mobile Service Providers (MSPs) must overcome significant hurdles, including the need for more efficient network management, the integration of new services, and the assurance of service quality. These challenges are being addressed by leveraging Software-Defined Networking (SDN) and Network Function Virtualization (NFV) to create a more agile and adaptable network architecture. This paper presents a novel, SDN-driven architecture designed to support the deployment of 5G services. The proposed solution utilizes a hybrid cloud environment, combining private and public resources to ensure the scalability and flexibility required for next-generation networks.

The Okubo-Weiss (OW) criterion is a standard tool for analyzing the relative strengths of vorticity generation and deformation in two-dimensional fluid flows. This study extends the OW criterion into three dimensions by examining the vorticity stretching mechanism, thereby creating a new three-dimensional version. We apply this new criterion to a three-dimensional turbulent flow to generate a corresponding OW map. The findings indicate that the three-dimensional version reveals distinct dynamical characteristics compared to the two-dimensional one. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the three-dimensional criterion can be utilized to identify coherent structures within the flow.

Lee-Wick theories, which feature distinctive non-physical poles in propagators, offer a viable framework for constructing renormalizable quantum field theories. This study examines the vacuum stability of such a theory, specifically a scalar model with a complex scalar field and a fermionic field. Our results indicate that the presence of Lee-Wick fields can either enhance or diminish vacuum stability, contingent upon the specific coupling constants.

While Neural Style Transfer (NST) has achieved significant success, existing methods often struggle to balance content and style representations, leading to content distortion. To address this, we introduce a new framework that leverages the complementary strengths of both visual and semantic features. Specifically, we utilize a feature fusion module to integrate visual features from a pre-trained VGG network with semantic features from a pre-trained ResNet model. This approach ensures that content integrity is maintained without compromising stylistic transfer. Additionally, we employ a multi-scale feature extraction module to capture style representations across various scales, enhancing the model's ability to perform fine-grained style transfer. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets confirm that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art techniques in NST.

This study examines the impact of geometric optimization on the work dissipation within finite-time thermodynamic protocols. We demonstrate that the proposed geometric optimization method is universally applicable to any protocol, regardless of the system's Hamiltonian, initial state, or specific geometric characteristics. Furthermore, we establish that dissipations resulting from optimized protocols are bounded by the system's geometric properties, offering a quantitative metric for the maximum efficiency attainable in geometrically optimized processes. Additionally, we illustrate that the dissipation reduction achieved by this approach can be amplified by adjusting the speed of the protocol. Finally, we validate these theoretical findings through numerical simulations of a two-level system.

This study investigates the production of a vector-like top quark partner, denoted as $T$, in association with a $Z$ boson at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). The analysis covers two distinct decay modes for the $Z$ boson: the leptonic channel ($Z \to \ell^+\ell^-$) and the hadronic channel ($Z \to jj$). Additionally, we examine the impact of various selection criteria on the signal significance and the resulting limits on the $T$ quark mass.

This study examines the stability of an interface separating two immiscible fluids subjected to an acoustic field. We analyze the Rayleigh-Taylor instability within a framework that accounts for both acoustic forcing and interfacial tension. The investigation focuses on a two-dimensional configuration where the fluids possess distinct densities and sound speeds. By applying a perturbation method, we derive the dispersion relation for the interface. Our results indicate that acoustic forcing can either stabilize or destabilize the system, contingent upon the specific values of the fluid properties. Furthermore, we demonstrate that interfacial tension plays a critical role in determining stability, with its effects varying based on the acoustic forcing parameters.

This paper investigates the finite-dimensional finite-pole cases of a class of complex interpolation spaces defined on the unit disk, specifically focusing on the relationship between these interpolation spaces and a reproducing kernel Hilbert space of holomorphic functions. We demonstrate that the finite-dimensional finite-pole subspace of this reproducing kernel Hilbert space corresponds exactly to the intersection of all intermediate spaces within the complex interpolation scale connecting the unit disk's $H^\infty$ space and its dual.

This study examines the production of exotic particles, including antiprotons, photons, and neutrons, generated by irradiating high-Z targets with photons and charged particles. The research utilizes a novel theoretical framework that integrates the relativistic quantum molecular dynamics (RQMD) model with the relativistic transport model (RTM) to simulate the entire process of particle generation and subsequent transport. The analysis specifically investigates the impact of varying target thickness and incident beam energy on the resulting particle yields.

This study introduces a new framework for event detection that leverages the syntactic dependency graph of input text. By utilizing this graph, the model incorporates both local and global contextual information to enhance detection performance. Specifically, it employs a graph convolutional network to aggregate relevant features from neighboring nodes within the dependency structure. Experimental results across three distinct datasets demonstrate that the proposed method surpasses current state-of-the-art approaches.

This paper introduces a new class of Markov chains that exhibit geometric ergodicity in a geometric sense. We apply this framework to analyze the ergodic properties of the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm within a specific type of non-compact target distribution.
We introduce a novel method for generating GHZ states in a three-qubit system, where the protocol relies on a specific Hamiltonian that is independent of time.

This work introduces a methodology for analyzing nonlinear dynamical systems perturbed by random noise, utilizing transfer operators to derive both statistical and dynamical characteristics. The transfer operator for these stochastic systems is defined as the convolution of the deterministic transfer operator with the noise's probability density function. We establish the existence and uniqueness of smooth invariant measures for such systems under conditions of uniform hyperbolicity and bounded noise. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the smoothness of these measures is directly linked to the smoothness of the noise density. The study also investigates the asymptotic behavior of time averages and the system's random asymptotic periodicity. Additionally, we derive upper bounds for the spectral radius of the transfer operator, which indicate exponential decay in the convergence of statistical measures. Finally, we apply this framework to the stochastic Lorenz system to compute its invariant measure and stochastic steady states.

This paper examines the propagation of high-frequency waves within a medium characterized by nonlinear absorption. We establish the validity of the geometric optics approximation and derive equations for the first- and second-order terms in our high-frequency expansion. Specifically, we prove that the residual error is bounded by $O(\omega^{-1})$.

Explainable reinforcement learning (XRL) aims to render learning agents more transparent and trustworthy by clarifying their decision-making processes. This paper presents a novel XRL framework designed to explain the decision-making of a specific reinforcement learning agent. The proposed method integrates two key components: a decision tree that captures the agent's learned policy, and a rule-based system that interprets the tree to generate explanations. The explanation generation process relies on a set of predefined rules that evaluate the agent's state and action to produce justifications. The system's efficacy is demonstrated through a case study involving a reinforcement learning agent trained to navigate a maze.

This paper examines the one-variable fragments of logics derived from combining modal extensions of classical and intuitionistic systems. We establish completeness for a corresponding intuitionistic modal logic and analyze decidability and complexity issues within both these one-variable fragments and their respective semantics.
We demonstrate that for Gaussian processes characterized by a Hurst parameter within the interval (1/4, 1), the expected signature serves as a complete identifier of the process.

This paper investigates the performance of 5G wireless cellular networks by leveraging angle-of-arrival (AOA) data for localization. We introduce a novel framework that integrates AOA measurements with a Markov chain model to estimate the position of a mobile user. This approach is designed to be computationally efficient and adaptable to diverse AOA measurement configurations. Furthermore, we derive a closed-form expression for the mean squared error (MSE) of the proposed estimator. Numerical simulations are conducted to assess the accuracy of this theoretical derivation and to evaluate the overall performance of the proposed method.

We establish that, in the Gross-Pitaevskii limit, the macroscopic wave function of a weakly interacting, uniform Bose-Einstein condensate at zero temperature corresponds to the minimizer of a specific non-linear Schrödinger energy. This finding extends prior work by the same author, which demonstrated convergence in the regime of large scattering length.

Image inpainting is a critical computer vision task that has seen significant recent advancements through deep learning. However, most current methods struggle with resolution changes, often producing subpar results when the input image is resized. This paper introduces a novel approach to image inpainting that explicitly accounts for resolution changes. Our method employs a two-stage process: first, the target image is upsampled to the desired resolution, and then a dedicated inpainting network fills in the missing regions. We further developed a new loss function to enhance the quality of upsampling, which in turn improves the overall final output. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing state-of-the-art inpainting techniques in scenarios involving resolution changes.

This study addresses the Thresholding Bandit problem, a scenario where an agent seeks to identify an unknown parameter $\theta$ within a set of $K$ candidates by querying them to determine if $\theta$ exceeds a specified threshold. We introduce a novel variant, the Stochastic Thresholding Bandit, which imposes two specific shape constraints: first, the unknown parameter is guaranteed to be one of two values, $\theta_1$ or $\theta_2$; and second, the query responses are monotonic with respect to the candidate indices. We demonstrate that this monotonicity allows for the construction of an algorithm that achieves a regret of $\mathcal{O}(\log T)$, surpassing the $\Omega(\sqrt{T})$ lower bound established for the standard Thresholding Bandit. Furthermore, we extend this framework to the Stochastic Multi-Armed Bandit (MAB) setting, proposing a method that attains $\mathcal{O}(\log T)$ regret for both stochastic and adversarial variants.
We demonstrate that NP equals coNP within the context of non-hamiltonian graphs, where the existence of Hamiltonian cycles is being queried.

This study examines the evolution of a hypersurface in a Riemannian manifold under the combined influence of mean curvature and extrinsic rigidity. We establish that, given appropriate conditions, the resulting geometric flow converges to a curve of constant mean curvature.

We examine the Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in a two-dimensional XY model using the winding number of circular paths. At low temperatures, the average squared winding number scales as $P^2 \sim \exp(-2\pi^2 J/T)$, where $J$ represents the spin-wave stiffness and $P$ denotes the circle's circumference. Conversely, at high temperatures, the same quantity follows a power law, $P^2 \sim P^{-\alpha}$, with $\alpha = 2\pi^2 T/\pi k_B T_c$. This behavior is derived from the vortex-antivortex pair correlation function, which is calculated by averaging over all possible circle perimeters.

The widespread adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) has sparked significant public debate regarding its advantages and drawbacks. This study examines the sentiments of Twitter users concerning AI by utilizing a novel dataset comprising 1.1 million tweets from 2018 to 2020. We employ a topic-aware sentiment analysis framework to identify both the specific issues discussed and the associated emotional responses. Our findings reveal four primary themes: (1) the advantages of AI, (2) the drawbacks of AI, (3) the future prospects of AI, and (4) the current state of AI. Furthermore, we observe that the "current state" theme is the most frequently addressed, while the "future" theme is the most polarized. We also note that the "advantages" theme is the most positively received, whereas the "drawbacks" theme is the most negatively perceived. Additionally, we observe that the "drawbacks" theme is the most prevalent among users in the US, while the "future" theme is the most popular in the UK.
